create.name: Pārāyana Vihāra
create.bio:
Pārāyana Vihāra is a small Theravada monastery for women in Port Townsend, on Washington's Olympic Peninsula, whose name means 'the way to the beyond'. Its spiritual director, the Welsh-born nun Ayya Ānandabodhī, trained for many years in the Thai Forest lineage of Ajahn Chah at Amaravati and Chithurst in England, then moved to the United States, where she took full bhikkhunī ordination in 2011 and co-founded the Aloka Vihara communities in San Francisco and later in the Sierra foothills. After the forest monastery closed in 2023 she came to Port Townsend on sabbatical, found a welcoming lay and monastic community there and decided to stay and found Pārāyana. A small group of resident nuns now share the life of practice with her.

The vihara tries to balance quiet monastic life with a welcome for visitors. On Sundays the public can come for a shared meal offering and an afternoon of chanting, meditation and Dhamma, and there is a Wednesday evening puja of sitting and chanting. Visitors may also use its Buddhist library, offer food, join the Saturday almsround or attend a retreat. The community lives on dana, keeps a three-month rains retreat and a winter retreat each year, and shares its talks on YouTube and its chanting online.

free_resources.title: Sunday at the Vihara
free_resources.description: The weekly open day: a shared meal offering to the nuns around eleven, tea and conversation, then an afternoon programme of chanting, sitting and Dhamma reflection. Everyone is welcome; the library stays open afterwards.

free_resources.title: Wednesday Evening Puja
free_resources.description: The community's regular evening practice of meditation and devotional chanting, open to visitors; cushions, benches and chairs are provided.

free_resources.title: Chanting
free_resources.description: Downloadable recordings and texts of the daily morning and evening chants in Pali and English, and a recollection of the early arahant nuns.

free_resources.title: Learn: Dhamma Resources
free_resources.description: A starting list of foundational Buddhist readings, material on women in Buddhism and books by the community's teachers.
